mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL annualized growth exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past three months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) over the past six months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where RSAFS shows sustained growth.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past month signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over the past month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a robust labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k & UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% over the past month, it signals tightening monetary conditions, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Housing Starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over the past three months signals a weakening in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where HOUST decreases by more than 10%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real GDP (GDPC1) over the past six months signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 shows sustained growth.
